plan.title: Add greenfield support to festina-create-project
plan.overview: Enhance festina-create-project with a greenfield detection branch that diverges after title capture. When greenfield is detected (no substantive product/engineering docs), the skill runs adaptive vision capture (2-4 broad questions), launches 4 parallel Explore subagents for research (stack, features, architecture, pitfalls), proposes versioned requirements (v1/v2/out-of-scope), and decomposes from v1 only. The brownfield path remains as an untouched else-branch. Research findings are stored in a new <research> section in project.xml. festina-define is removed entirely from all locations.

approach.rationale:
The greenfield flow is inserted as a conditional branch after the existing get_project_title step. Greenfield detection checks product/engineering dirs for substantive docs (empty or overview-only counts as greenfield). This branching approach means the brownfield path is never touched — the existing socratic_qa, search_product_docs, search_engineering_docs, validate_requirements steps remain byte-for-byte identical in the else branch.
The parallel research agent pattern follows festina-scope's established approach (apps/festinalente/src/content/skills/festina-scope/SKILL.md:280-348) — 4 Explore subagents launched via Agent tool in a single message for parallelism. Each agent uses WebSearch for real-world research rather than codebase exploration (since there's no codebase to explore).
Vision capture uses the existing AskUserQuestion dialogue pattern (apps/festinalente/src/content/skills/festina-create-project/SKILL.md:62) — one question at a time with propose-then-validate flow.
festina-define removal is a clean delete — per directive R1, no re-exports, no compatibility shims, no deprecation markers. All 6 locations are updated in a single task.
Source edits follow directive F1: all skill/template changes go in apps/festinalente/src/content/, not in .claude/ or .festinalente/ installed output.

task.name: Add greenfield detection and vision capture to create-project skill

contract.postcondition: If greenfield detected, vision capture completes with 2-4 questions; if brownfield, existing flow runs unchanged

contract.precondition: User is in any step of the greenfield flow
contract.postcondition: On cancellation, no project or task files created; on agent failure, flow continues with remaining results

task.action:
- After the existing get_project_title step (line 72), add a new detect_greenfield step: - Use node .festinalente/scripts/festinalente.cjs list-product and list-engineering - Greenfield = product dir has 0 docs (or only overview.md) AND engineering dir has 0 docs (or only overview.md) - Detection is deterministic, no user confirmation needed - Output: set isGreenfield flag
- After detect_greenfield, add a conditional branch: - If NOT greenfield (brownfield): continue to existing socratic_qa step unchanged - If greenfield: run greenfield_vision_capture step instead of socratic_qa
- greenfield_vision_capture step (replaces socratic_qa for greenfield): - Question 1 (required): "What are you building? Describe the core idea in a few sentences." Use AskUserQuestion with header "Vision", free-form input - Question 2 (required): "What tech stack do you want to use, or are you unsure?" Use AskUserQuestion with options: common stacks + "Unsure" + "Other" - Question 3 (required): "What's the MVP — the minimum that makes this useful? And what's explicitly NOT in v1?" Use AskUserQuestion with header "MVP Scope", free-form input - Question 4 (optional/skippable): "Anything else I should know? (Skip if nothing)" Use AskUserQuestion with options: "Skip" + "Other" for free input
- Handle cancellation: If user cancels at any point during vision capture, output "Cancelled. No files created." and exit. No partial state left behind.
- Handle minimal input (FR11): If user provides only a title and skips all questions, the AI uses judgment to infer vision, tech, and MVP scope from the title alone. All inferred items are marked as "(inferred)" in the requirements later.
- The brownfield path (existing socratic_qa through acceptance_criteria_validation) must remain byte-for-byte identical — wrap it in the else branch of the greenfield check.
- Also wrap search_product_docs and search_engineering_docs steps in the brownfield branch (greenfield has no docs to search — research agents handle this instead).
task.done: Running /festina-create-project on a project with no product/engineering docs triggers the greenfield vision capture flow; running on a project with existing docs triggers the unchanged brownfield flow

task.name: Add parallel research agents for greenfield flow

contract.precondition: Vision capture completed with user's input (title, optional tech prefs, MVP scope)
contract.postcondition: 4 research agents complete (or gracefully degrade on failure); findings stored in project.xml research section

task.action:
- After greenfield_vision_capture, add greenfield_research step - Launch 4 parallel Explore subagents using Agent tool in a SINGLE message:
1. **Stack Researcher** (subagent_type="Explore"): - If user specified tech: validate choice, research best practices, augment with complementary tools - If user said "unsure": propose 2-3 stack options with pros/cons for the specific project type - Use WebSearch to find current best practices, popular libraries, deployment options - Output: recommended stack with rationale
2. **Feature Researcher** (subagent_type="Explore"): - Based on vision and MVP scope, research similar products/projects - Identify common features for this type of application - Categorize as "essential for MVP" vs "nice to have" vs "future" - Use WebSearch to find feature lists of comparable products - Output: categorized feature list with rationale
3. **Architecture Researcher** (subagent_type="Explore"): - Based on stack and features, research architectural patterns - Recommend project structure, key patterns (state management, routing, etc.) - Consider scalability and maintainability for the project type - Use WebSearch to find architecture guides for the chosen stack - Output: recommended architecture with rationale
4. **Pitfall Researcher** (subagent_type="Explore"): - Research common mistakes and gotchas for this project type + stack - Identify security concerns, performance pitfalls, UX anti-patterns - Use WebSearch to find "mistakes to avoid" content - Output: categorized pitfall list with mitigations
- All 4 agents always launch regardless of user input (contract C2 invariant) - Handle agent failure (FR10): wrap each agent result collection in error handling. If an agent fails or returns empty results, log which agent failed, continue with remaining results, and inform the user: "Note: {agent name} research was unavailable." - After all agents complete, synthesize findings into a summary for the user - If user said "unsure" about tech (FR4): present stack agent's proposals with pros/cons and ask user to validate/choose using AskUserQuestion - Store all findings in the project.xml <research> section when writing project file
Note: These are Explore subagents with WebSearch capability, NOT codebase exploration (there's no codebase to explore for greenfield). The skill's frontmatter already includes WebSearch in allowed-tools.
task.done: After greenfield vision capture, 4 parallel research agents launch, complete (or gracefully degrade), and findings are synthesized for user review

task.name: Add versioned requirements and v1-only decomposition for greenfield

contract.precondition: Research findings available from all successful agents
contract.postcondition: Requirements proposed as v1 (MVP) / v2 (future) / out-of-scope; decomposition uses only v1 requirements

task.action:
- After greenfield_research, add greenfield_requirements step:
1. AI proposes requirements based on research findings and vision capture: - v1 (MVP): Core requirements that deliver the minimum useful product - v2 (future): Enhancements and nice-to-haves for later - out-of-scope: Explicitly excluded from this project entirely - If user provided minimal input (FR11), mark all as "(inferred)"
2. Present to user via AskUserQuestion: - Header: "Proposed Requirements" - Show all three categories clearly formatted - Options: "Approve", "Adjust", "You decide"
3. User validates and can: - Move items between categories (v1 ↔ v2 ↔ out-of-scope) - Add or remove requirements - Accept as-is
4. After validation, store all three categories in project.xml: - v1 requirements become the numbered R1-Rn requirements - v2 requirements stored in <notes> as "v2 (future): ..." - out-of-scope stored in <scope><out-of-scope>
5. Decomposition uses ONLY v1 requirements (contract C3 invariant): - Pass only v1 (R1-Rn) to the existing decompose_tasks step - v2 and out-of-scope are stored but never decomposed into tasks
- After requirements are set, flow merges back to the existing validate_requirements step, then continues through decompose_tasks → confirm_decomposition → write_tasks as normal (these steps work on R1-Rn regardless of greenfield/brownfield).
- When writing project.xml (write_project_xml step), also populate the <research> section with findings from the 4 research agents.
task.done: AI proposes versioned requirements from research findings; user validates; only v1 requirements are decomposed into tasks; v2 and out-of-scope stored in project.xml but not decomposed

testing.regression: - Existing brownfield create-project flow unchanged - All other skills still compile (festina-define removal doesn't break partials) - Config.yaml template still valid after festina-define removal - Git directive still valid after G-DEFPROD removal

case.scenario: User provides only a title and skips all vision capture questions

edge-cases.case: AI infers vision, tech preferences, and MVP scope from title alone; all proposed requirements marked as "(inferred)"; research agents use title as sole input
Exit immediately with message, no project.xml or task.xml files created, no partial state left behind

case.scenario: One or more research agents fail or return empty results

edge-cases.case: Flow continues with remaining agent results; user is informed which research was unavailable; requirements are proposed from available research only
Stack research agent proposes 2-3 options with pros/cons; user validates choice via AskUserQuestion before proceeding to other agents' synthesis

case.scenario: Product dir has only overview.md (no substantive docs)

edge-cases.case: Treated as greenfield — overview.md alone is not considered substantive documentation
Existing 6+ task warning applies — user can proceed, split project, or reduce scope (same as brownfield flow)

case.scenario: User moves all requirements to v2/out-of-scope during validation

edge-cases.case: No v1 requirements means nothing to decompose — prompt user that at least one v1 requirement is needed

pitfall.issue: Editing installed output instead of source

The brownfield path must remain as an untouched else-branch. Do not refactor the existing socratic_qa or search steps — simply wrap them in the brownfield conditional.

pitfall.issue: Handlebars compilation breaking from new content

pitfalls.pitfall: New steps must use valid Handlebars-compatible Markdown. Avoid literal {{ or }} in content that isn't a partial reference — escape if needed.
Run comprehensive grep for 'festina-define' across entire repo before marking task 5 complete to catch any obscure references.

pitfall.issue: Research agent prompts too vague for greenfield

pitfalls.pitfall: Agent prompts must include the user's vision, tech preferences, and MVP scope as concrete context — not just the title. Each agent needs enough input to produce useful research.

pitfall.issue: project.xml template change affecting existing projects

pitfalls.pitfall: The new <research> section is additive — existing project.xml files without it will still parse fine. The template is only used for new projects.
